title: Production GRU Attention Baseline for WLASL30
research_question: Can a bidirectional GRU with temporal attention classify isolated WLASL30 signs from one-hand MediaPipe landmarks with thesis-ready accuracy?
input_representation: MediaPipe hand landmarks flattened per frame
preprocessing: Uniformly sample or pad each sequence to 64 frames
Extract one detected hand with 21 landmarks per frame
Fill missing detections with interpolation and edge values
Normalize each frame by wrist origin and wrist-to-middle-finger scale
Flatten 21 landmarks with 3 coordinates into 63 features per frame

runtime.notes: Runtime was not recorded in final_assault/final_results.json

robust_reference.notes: Five-fold validation on WLASL100 filtered to the same 30 classes is the stronger thesis reference.

main_findings: GRU + Temporal Attention is the strongest individual model in the final_assault comparison.
The model reaches 58.82% Top-1 and 91.18% Top-5 on the WLASL30 test split.
The later five-fold evaluation provides a stronger reference result: 63.85% Top-1 mean and 86.46% Top-5 mean.
limitations: The single test split contains only 34 samples, so the reported test result has high variance.
Macro F1 and balanced accuracy were not computed for this run.
Detection-rate statistics were not saved in the original experiment artifacts.
Only one hand is represented, which can miss two-hand and non-manual sign information.
next_actions: Use this manifest format for the 32/64/96 frame-length sweep.
Add normalized confusion matrices and per-class accuracy files for final models.
Record detection-rate statistics in future landmark extraction and evaluation runs.
normalization_strategy: Wrist-centered coordinates scaled by wrist-to-middle-finger distance
interpolation_strategy: Linear interpolation between valid frames with edge fill at sequence boundaries
